panels.figure_caption: Patients here reported. In A) we observe the proband clinical features; In B) we observe the proband’s sister clinical features.
in_text_mentions: Patient 1, the proband, aged 14 years and 8 months, was born from non-consanguineous and healthy parents (Figure 1A). After a normal pregnancy, the patient was born at term by cesarean section, weighing 2,900 g (25th-50th centile), length and head circumference were not informed. His developmental progress was delayed; he sat at 1 year old, he is not able to walk. At the age of 9 months, he began to have seizures and has been on valproic acid with good control. Unlike typical AS patients, he did not display a happy disposition with frequent smiling and laughing. He has normal EEG and brain MRI

Patient 2, the proband’s sister, aged 6 years and 3 months, was born from non-consanguineous and healthy parents (Figure 1B); these two siblings have different fathers (Figure 2). The prenatal period was uneventful and the baby was delivered by cesarean section at full term with a birth weight of 3385 g (50th-75th centile), height of 50 cm (50th-75th centile), and head circumference of 35 cm (75th-90th centile). panels.rationale: Real clinical photograph of an 8-month-old boy with Angelman syndrome (and Klinefelter syndrome) showing facial dysmorphism; captioned broad nasal root and thin upper lip, with in-text description of wide mouth matching an Angelman facial feature. No Klinefelter-specific manifestation is visible in this facial view.
panels.attribution_text: Sánchez et al. Atypical Association of Angelman Syndrome and Klinefelter Syndrome in a Boy with 47,XXY Karyotype and Deletion 15q11.2-q13.. Case reports in genetics 2014. doi:10.1155/2014/517091. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Facial appearance. Dysmorphic features, broad nasal root, and thin upper lip.
in_text_mentions: At 8 months his head circumference was 46 cm (p75), weight 9,555 g (p90), and height 70 cm (p75–p90). He showed delayed acquisition of motor skills, he could not remain seated or handle objects, and axial hypotonia was observed. He showed dysmorphic features, occipital flattening, a thin upper lip, a wide mouth, tongue protrusion, a broad nasal root, and divergent strabismus (Figure 1). A brain MRI showed a structurally normal brain.
